[The Arśaḥkuṭhāra Elixir: Take the best dantī, two parts of agni, trikaṭuka, halinī, pīlu, and kumbha; having cooked these in one prastha of urine, along with the milk of snuhī, add one pala of the juice, two palas of sulphur, three palas of iron, a kuḍava of copper, and five parts each of powdered alkali and ash. Place this in a vessel and cook it over a blazing fire; this powder is the "Axe for Hemorrhoids" (Arśaḥkuṭhāra). VR 15.61.
[The Essence of the Ornament of the Three Worlds: The essence produced from black vajra-clouds, purified with glass and borax,
having been liquefied, reduced to powder, and roasted with ghee— VRrs_15.62.
Then, one should coat it with a powder consisting of one-eighth part of grain and roast it three times;
thereafter, one should roast it three times with a wick made from royal resin mixed with the juice of *luṅga*.
And four times with the juices of *varṣābhū*, *vāsā*, and *matsyākṣikā*, and diligently thirty times with decoctions of *guggulu* and the three myrobalans (*triphalā*).
With a collyrium produced from equal parts of juice and fragrance, taking one-eighth part [of the mercury],
one should roast it fifty times, grinding it between each roasting.
Having purified it, rendered it fluid, and processed it with a lovely essence, one should grind it with ghee and roast it eight times with mercury combined with the juice of *lakucha*.
Likewise, one should properly recite the pure *tāra* ten times with the substance called *manohvā*,
and likewise twenty times with *balin*, fish-eyes, and juices.
Having processed it ten times with copper combined with the ghee of a black cow,
one should then roast that mixture of equal parts in the juice of *nirguṇḍī*.
One should then roast it ten times with a kajjalī produced from its own juice and smell;
into that, one should add a portion equal to one-eighth of the weight of the vaikrānta ash.
Having ground all that together with an equal portion of *rājāvarta* powder, one should then saturate it with the juice of fresh ginger.
[One may prepare it] with the fresh juice of *guḍūcī*, or with the juice of *bhūkadambara*,
or with the juice of *bhṛṅgarāja*, or with the juice of *citramūla*.
Then, having again prepared a powder from the three pungents (vyoṣa), gañjā, and the tubers of the kanda plant with a moist liquid, one should place it in a clean casket.
This very [elixir] is renowned as the ornament of the three worlds and the best of all elixirs;
it removes all diseases and is proclaimed by the illustrious Śambhu.
It causes upward movement of wind (udāvarta), constipation, abdominal pain, hoarseness,
dullness of intellect, colic, and even sterility.
It destroys all types of urinary disorders without exception, as well as various kinds of colic, and even the most severe colic known as *pariṇāma-śūla*.
It also cures blood-born swellings (raktagulma) and unbearable menstrual pain (rajaḥśūla) in women;
the appropriate after-drink and wholesome diet should be administered according to the specific nature of each disease.
[The general application: Vacā, hiṅgu, viḍaṅga, rock salt, jīraka, nāgara, marica, pippalī, kuṣṭha, pathyā, citraka, and ajamodaka. VR 15.77.
A powder with progressively increasing quantities of ingredients and double the amount of jaggery should be taken;
one karṣa of it should be drunk after with warm water for the conquest of hemorrhoids caused by vāta.
One should powder together equal parts of processed iron, indrayava, ginger, bhallātaka, citraka, the marrow of bilva, viḍaṅga, and pathyā.
Equal amounts of sugar should be added; by consuming one *karṣa* of this, one conquers hemorrhoids.
For the pacification of phlegmatic hemorrhoids (*śleṣmārśas*), Ānandabhairava should be administered;
indeed, that should be given as three *guñjās*, equal to dead copper (*mṛtatāmra*).
One should cook the tender leaves of the *kusumbha* plant with *kāñjika* alone;
one should eat them daily like a vegetable for the pacification of the disease of hemorrhoids.
[General Application: Seeds of *devadālī* finely powdered with rock salt (*saindhava*) and applied as a paste with fermented rice-gruel (*āranāla*) destroy root diseases. (VR 15.82)
A plaster made of *kāñcanī* flowers, powdered conch shell, and realgar,
applied with the juice of *gajapippalī*, is indeed an axe for hemorrhoids.
One should perform cleansing with the decoction of *devadālī* to destroy hemorrhoids;
even the prolapse of the rectum will be pacified by this, and not otherwise.
Bitter gourd (kaṭutumbikā) with its seeds ground together with fermented rice-scum (āranāla) and mixed with jaggery, when applied as a plaster,
destroys hemorrhoids along with their very roots.
A wick soaked in *pīlu* oil and inserted into the anus quickly destroys hemorrhoids as well as all associated pain.
An ointment made of *arka* latex, the stem of *snuhī*, pungent *lābu* leaves,
and *karañja* mixed with goat’s urine is beneficial for bleeding hemorrhoids.
An ointment made from the roots of the śigru plant and the leaves of the arka plant is beneficial for hemorrhoids.
When provoked by dry *kodrava*, aged *mudga*, and *caṇaka* beans, the wind (vāyu) moves downward; having obstructed the passage and dried up the impurity, it causes retention of feces and urine.

Then, moving upward, it surely and incessantly brings about *udāvarta* out of its agitation, producing pain in the heart, back, abdomen, bladder, and head, along with dyspnea, cough, and fever. (VRs 16.1)
Having made a paste of kaṅkuṣṭha, hiṅgu, siṃdhūttha, trivṛt, daṃtī, vacā, abhayā, and the root of citraka, one should cook ghee [with these].
Snuhī-milk mixed in a fourfold quantity of cow’s milk,
when drunk at all times, destroys upward-moving wind (udāvarta) and abdominal diseases.
[Diarrhea:

Due to excessive drinking of water, eating sesame flour, sprouted grains, dry or parched meat, overeating, constipation, or intestinal worms, the wind (vāyu), having become provoked, prepares for excessive evacuation; it does so by suppressing the digestive fire (agni) and loosening the waste matter as well as the watery constituents of the body.
The juice of the *dardura* (frog), finely ground into a sharp powder and mixed in equal parts with mercury (*rasendra*),
rubbed with the juice of *kāñcanāra*, destroys all types of diarrhea.
This mercury, known as Dardura, is ground with equal parts of a sharp [substance] and processed with Kāñcanāra water; when cooked in a *puṭa* vessel, it cures diarrhea.
One should grind together equal parts of cinnabar, vatsanābha poison, black pepper, borax, and long pepper; this is indeed the Ānandabhairava elixir.
Having ascertained the patient's strength, one should administer either one *guñjā* or half a *guñjā*;
thereafter, one should have them lick the fruit and bark of *kuṭaja* with honey.
One karṣa of this powder conquers diarrhea arising from the three doṣas. As wholesome diet, one should administer curd-rice, cow’s ghee, or even buttermilk.
For thirst, cold water is beneficial, and Vijayā is recommended at night.
Having melted one *pala* of collyrium produced from sulphur, realgar, and mercury— each weighing one *pala* separately— one should add one *pala* of "sky" (*vyoma*) that has lost its luster.
Having stirred all that with a wooden spoon, one should throw it into *kuṭaja* leaves;
then, having ground it again with effort, one should subsequently soak it.
With the juices of the *bālatindu* fruit, as well as with *audumbara* milks,
the sap of *aralu* bark, and likewise with the fresh juice of *dugdhinī*, [one should perform the treatment].
With the auspicious juices of pomegranates cooked in a closed vessel (*puṭapāka*),
with the juices of the root of black *kāmbojikā*, and with those derived from the bark of *kuṭaja*.
One should add two palas each of the powders of Tulyāṃśā, Viśvagandhārī, Musta, Vatsaka, Dīpyā, Agnimocā, Sāra, and Jīraka.
One should add one karṣa each of vatsanābha and [the other ingredients] to that,
powder them, and then saturate the mixture seven times with a decoction of ginger.
When the mercury has been thus perfected and ground, one should place it in a casket;
it is known as Sudhāsāra, possessing a luster equal to the essence of nectar.
It is digestive, carminative, constipating, cordial, and likewise an appetizer;
it overcomes even the three humors and diarrhea that are difficult to conquer with other medicines.

It instantly checks undigested food, as well as blood-redness, fever, dysentery, and cholera accompanied by diarrhea— just as the transgression of one who is honored obstructs the arising of the fruit of merit.
Having indeed formed a pill from the paste of *viśvā* and water with the best of juices (*rasottama*),
one should place it in a *svedanīyantra* and cook it for the duration of half a *ghaṭikā*.
Having drawn it up and crushed it with those very waters, one should extract the juice;
then, having added an amount equal to coriander seeds of the essence of nectar (sudhāsāra), [one should proceed].
In the aforementioned diseases, the best of physicians should administer wholesome,
beneficial, and moderate food with buttermilk or curd.
The young fruit of the plantain, the gurvī fruit, the bilva fruit,
as well as the mango pulp, madhuka, and eggplant are recommended.

This supreme elixir (rasottama), when administered during the stage of undigested waste (āmapāka), immediately destroys all types of diarrhea, malabsorption syndrome (grahaṇī), hiccup, weak digestion, abdominal distension, and loss of appetite; it does so within two or three applications.
When a cloth is tied over the mouth of a saṃbu vessel and a substance to be cooked is placed inside,
and it is then covered and cooked, that is called a *svedanī* apparatus.
[The Elixir of Lokeśvara:
One should combine two parts of sulfur and eight parts of powdered conch shell;
then one should grind a single part of mercury with the milk of the *arka* plant. (VR 16.25)
Having dried it thus repeatedly with the liquid of *citraka*,
one should then combine it with mercury and add half as much alkali.
One should prepare pills with the milk of the *arka* plant and then dry them;
having sealed them in a vessel smeared with powder, one should then apply the *puṭa* fire.
This is indeed the essence of Lokeśvara, which destroys diseases of the digestive tract (grahaṇī).
One should administer four *guñjā* seeds of it together with black pepper and clarified butter; likewise, curd and boiled rice constitute the wholesome diet for Lokeśvara.
[The Essence of the Lord of the World:
One part of dead mercury and four parts of pure sulfur should be ground in a mortar for one *yāma*; with that, the previously mentioned cowries should be treated.
Having ground ṭaṅkaṇa with the milk of cows, one should smear it on the mouths of cowrie shells;
having carefully sealed them in a vessel, one should cook them in a *puṭa*.
Having extracted them while they are still warm from their own heat and then powdered the cowries,
one should take four *guñjā* measures of the substance known as Lokanātharasa along with honey.
A decoction composed of nāgara, ativiṣā, mustā, devadāru, and vacā,
taken as an after-drink (anupāna), destroys vāta-type diarrhea.
One should prepare a smooth collyrium paste using one *pala* each of nāga-ash, mercury, and the fragrance of the sky (*vyomagaṃdha*); immediately thereafter, one should add [the other ingredients].
In a mixture of two *pala*s of quicksilver (*druta*) with an equal amount of mercury (*alā*),
it should be thoroughly blended with roasted *yakṣākṣa*, *siṃhūttha*, *vacā*, the three pungents (*vyoṣa*), and the two types of *jīraka*.
One should mix the previous paste with equal parts of *sapathyā*, *vijayā*, and *dīpyā* that have been finely powdered, and subsequently macerate it.
With the essences of the bark of the great *nimba* tree, the juices of the roots of *kāmbhojī*,
and the extracts of *nāgabalā* and *guḍūcī*— each prepared three times—
one should then fashion pills the size of a jujube stone.
Indeed, the *nāgasundara* elixir, when consumed in a dose of one *valla*,
will surely destroy various diseases of dysentery, as well as prolapse of the rectum and *biṃbiśī*.
[Six-niṣka Oil]: Six niṣkas of sesame oil, one niṣka of jambīra juice,
and five guñjās of salt— one should rub these firmly with the fingers.
One should lick [the medicine] which destroys the essence of suffering from rheumatism (āmavāta), and follow the wholesome regimen as previously prescribed.
The *saṃgrahaṇī* repeatedly collects the waste and sometimes causes its excessive discharge;
loss of appetite, swelling, and lethargy are the symptoms of the disease of *grahaṇī*.
[Vajrakapāṭarasa]:
Dead mercury, mica, sulphur, barley-alkali, and borax,
along with *vacā*, *jayā*, and *jayantī*— all these in equal parts— with the juices of *bhṛṅgarāja*.
One should grind it with citron for three days and dry that ball;
then one should gently steam it for half a watch (three hours) over a mild fire in an iron vessel.
When the consistency of the paste is equalized, one should add *niśā* and *mocarasa*;
then one should saturate it seven times with the juices of *vijayā*, drying and grinding it each time.
This is the *vajrakapāṭa* elixir; one should lick half a *niṣka* of it with honey.
[The Elixir of the Fire-Boy (Agnikumārarasa):
Having ground burnt cowrie shells together with the three pungents (tryūṣaṇa), borax, poison, sulphur, and purified mercury—all in equal parts—with the juices of *jambīra* fruits; VR 16.43.
One should rub [the medicine] and eat a māṣa measure, and afterwards lick black pepper with ghee.
This cures the disease of *grahaṇī*; as a wholesome diet, buttermilk with rice is beneficial.
Cinnabar, black pepper, sulphur, long pepper, borax, and poison,
along with the seeds of *kanaka*— these in equal parts [should be processed] with the juices of *vijayā*.
One should grind it for exactly one *yāma* or even for just a moment and form it into pills; when consumed, this "Golden Beauty" (*kanakasundara*) elixir destroys chronic diarrhea (*grahaṇī*).
It destroys sluggish digestion, acute fever, and diarrhea;
one should prescribe curd-rice as wholesome food, or indeed buttermilk made from cow’s or goat’s milk.
[The Mercury-Remover Elixir (Grahaṇīhararasa):
Mercury, mica, and sulphur, in increasing proportions, should be ground for three days with the juice of *jayā*.
One should administer half a *gadyāṇaka* of this together with honey; the regimen of wholesome food consists of curd and boiled rice.
The seed of Maheśvara situated in cinnabar (hiṅgula) should be extracted by means of the *pāta* apparatus;
it is then combined with equal parts of sulphur, potassium carbonate, mercury, and mica, along with *kokilākṣa*, in an iron mortar.

This medicinal paste (valla), combined with cumin and fresh ginger, should be applied as an ointment over a fire that is smokeless and free of flames; it remains effective at drying up fluids for as long as it stays there.

This king of elixirs (rasarāja), proclaimed by Vāsudeva, destroys fevers arising from deranged humors, excessive discharges, abdominal tumors, and the entire host of hemorrhoids; it is the sole bolt that bars the gate against the disease of violent constipation.
[Laghusiddhābhrakarasa:
Take equal parts of purified mercury, sulphur, mica, and realgar;
having placed them in an iron mortar, combine them with cow’s clarified butter.
One should carefully place the mortar upon a charcoal-heated iron pan in a trough-shaped furnace,
and then grind it with an iron pestle for two days.
Thus, this mercury-king (rasendra) is established; it is considered light-siddha-abhraka.
At dawn, a dose equal to a *valla* of this mercury, taken with water infused with cumin, [is effective].
When drunk, it swiftly removes even the most obstinate *grahaṇī*,
as well as most terrible diarrhea and fever accompanied by diarrhea.
It is digestive, appetizing, heart-pleasing, and brings lightness to the body;
it was taught by Nāgārjuna as that which produces immediate conviction.
[The Essence of All Diseases: Having melted one *pala* of mercury combined with an equal amount of purified lead in an iron vessel, one should cast it into the earth along with oil.
Then, having cast it into molten sulphur and stirred it thoroughly,
one should cast it again into an iron vessel, melt it, and pour it out.
One should digest an equal amount of cinnabar (tāla), then, having again pulverized it as before,
one should properly digest an equal amount of well-purified red ochre (kunaṭī).
When that has been pulverized, one should add an equal amount of niruttha lead;
likewise, one should add an equal amount of all other ingredients, including dead iron pyrite (mṛtatāpya).
One karṣa each of sharp iron filings, kharpara, vyomābhraka, hiṅgula, śilājatu, the six pungents (ṣaṭkoṭha), kaṭphala, and miśī; ||| VR 16.61 ||
Dīpyaka, the four spices (caturjāta), reṇuka, uśīra, vellaka, tuṃburu, bhārṅgikā, rāsnā, kaṅkola, and corapuṣkara.
Two palas each of riṅgiṇī, ciratikta, and the seeds of unmattaka,
and a twelfth part of each of all these [other ingredients] along with two palas of lāṅgalī.
Then, having added a large amount of white vatsanābha,
one should subsequently [mix it] with a decoction of ten parts of the three myrobalans (triphalā).
Having processed [the ingredients] with the juices of *jayantī*, *ārdraka*, *vāsā*, and *mārkava*,
one should prepare pills the size of chickpeas.
One should consume a single pill; it produces an intense hunger and cures cholera, restlessness, and hiccup. It should be used as something sweet and cool.

This pill conquers in an instant all diseases— chronic dysentery, constant aching of the limbs, severe wasting, jaundice, pain born of wind, phlegm, or the three humors combined, as well as abdominal tumors, colic, hiccups, flatulence, cholera, cough, asthma, hemorrhoids, abscesses, and likewise any other ailments.
Having prepared a kajjalī of mercury and sulfur in equal proportions,
one should melt it in an iron vessel and then add an amount equal to the mercury.
One should place the ashes of moving and non-moving beings,
along with those derived from honey and combined with sulphur, into a vessel made of iron.
Then, having stirred it with a wooden stick, one should pour it onto a plantain leaf;
thereafter, having covered it and ground it into a powder, one should place it in an iron vessel.
One should cast into that [liquid] a measure of ash produced from honey,
along with one *pala* of "sky-ash" (*vyomabhasma*) that has been properly reduced to a state free of lunar spots.
Having made equal parts of *viṣa*, *viṣā*, *gandhārī*, *mocasāra*, and *jīraka*,
one should add half a part of these to the juice.
Having crushed all these together, one should cultivate [the ointment] with great effort,
using jayantī, mahārāṣṭrī, gañjākinī, and aśvagandhā.
Thereafter, one should prepare a powder with the decoction of five *kolakas*;
thus perfected, this elixir is known as *Grahaṇīgajakesarī*.
This elixir is called Nandin by name and Sudhānidhi (Treasury of Nectar) by its action;
it is measured with a *valla* of ginger smeared with clarified butter.
When consumed, it destroys chronic diarrhea (grahaṇī), just as association with the virtuous destroys discord;
in this case, wholesome food should be given along with a small amount of ghee, combined with curd and buttermilk.
It is wholesome, moderate in quantity, clear, light, easily digestible, and provides relish;
it is highly digestive, stimulates the appetite, destroys undigested matter (āma), and induces a desire for food.
Through the application of various medicinal formulations, it destroys all types of diarrhea;
even while binding the waste matter, it quickly does not cause abdominal distension in men.
[The Elixir of Swift Power]:
Mercury, sulfur, mica, iron, orpiment, realgar,
purified antimony, and vimala— each taken in equal parts.
Having made a collyrium paste with these, one should fry it with a small amount of oil;
[adding] granthika, jīraka, citra, dīpyaka, mustaka, and viṣa.
Having powdered equal parts of young mango, young bilva, and the core of the *moca* fruit,
one should add that paste in half the quantity as before.
One should again knead it with effort so that it becomes a single mass;
one should then meditate upon it for seven cycles with the decoction of the five *kolakas*.
One should also process it ten times with the juice of *aralu* bark;
by means of the prescribed sequence of application, this very elixir is indeed produced.

Indeed, that elixir known as Śīghraprabhāva, measured at half a niṣka, when consumed with the water of a snow-clad mountain, is for the disease of chronic diarrhea (grahaṇī), for the ailment of dysentery, for flatulence arising from grahaṇī, for loss of appetite, for wind-disorders, for weak digestion, for when the waste has been expelled, for further fears of moving humors, and for hiccups. (VR 16.84)
[The *poṭalī* elixir: One should take an equal amount of the paste of mercury and sulphur, along with an equal amount of dead iron (*mṛtaloha*) and borax (*ṭaṅkaṇa*).
Having ground these together for one day with the juice of *jayā*, and having crushed them into a fine powder, one should roast them in a crucible (*bhāṇḍa*).
And one should administer that medicinal packet for the cessation of the grahaṇī disorder characterized by the predominance of the three humors.
[Vahnijvālāvaṭīrasa:
Take one *māṣa* each of mercury and sulfur that have been reduced to a fine paste, and one *māṣa* of mica;
these should be rubbed with the acidic juice of *mātuluṅga*. (VR 16.87)
Having purified two māṣas each of the three pungents (tryūṣaṇa) separately seven times, as well as triśūlī, bhṛṅga, cāṅgerī, sātalā, and tīkṣṇaparṇikā; VRrs_16.88 //
Śvetāparājitā, Kanyā, Matsyākṣī, Grīṣmasundarā,
Karīṇī, Karṇamoṭī, Rudantī, Citrā, and Ārdrikā.
One should prepare pills the size of a black gram (māṣa) by grinding [the drug] separately with the juices of two palas each of *dhustūra*, *kākamācī*, and *musalī*.
When consumed with *vyoṣa* and *parṇakhaṇḍa* for the treatment of malabsorption (*grahaṇī*),
this pill— known by the name Vahnijvālā— is said to pacify loss of appetite, consumption (*rājayakṣman*), weak digestion, and the diseases of postpartum women.
[Vajradhararasa]: Mercury, sulfur, copper, mica, the three alkalis, varuṇa, vṛṣa, the alkali of *apāmārga*, and salt—two *māṣaka* each of these. (VRs 16.92)
One should cook the [drug] ground with the juices of *cāṅgerī* and *hastituṇḍī* in a *puṭapāka* vessel;
having then consumed a *guñjā* dose, one should drink *kāñjika* in cases of chronic diarrhea (*grahaṇī*).
In cases of colic pain, cough, and weak digestion, ginger juice is beneficial;
likewise, freshly drawn warm milk is effective for acid bile (amlapitta); indeed, he is the wielder of the thunderbolt.
[The Mercury-Lock Compound for the Grahani]:
Mercury, sulfur, ativiṣā, abhayā, mica, the two types of alkali, mocarasa, vacā, and jayā—ground with the juice of jambīra and formed into a bolus—this shall be the grahaṇīkapāṭa. (VR 16.95)

At dawn, one should lick half a māṣa of that [powder] with honey; one should consume the ashes of a śambūka shell along with clarified butter, honey, milk-yielding plants, cumin, māṇimanthā, and tīkṣṇā, and at first, eat a meal of curd.
[The Powder of Sauvarcala, etc.

One should take equal parts of sauvarcala salt, the two types of cumin, coriander, jayā, yavānī, long pepper, and ginger, along with the pulp of wood-apple (kapittha); having prepared this powder, it should be administered at night by those suffering from acute pitta disorders.
A single *gadyāṇa* measure, combined with honey, sugar-candy, and buttermilk, quickly pacifies loss of appetite;
furthermore, when wind or phlegm predominates, one should administer a decoction of *kuṭaja* at night.
[Mustādi powder: Musta, vatsaka, pāṭhā, agni, vyoṣa, prativiṣā, viṣa, dhātakī, the exudate of mocarasa, and mango stone—this [powder] cures disorders of the grahaṇī. (VRṢ 16.99)
One should grind together equal parts of fire (citraka), ginger, biḍa salt, bilva, and salt;
by drinking this with warm water afterwards, one conquers malabsorption (grahaṇī) arising from vāta.
One should have the patient lick equal parts of burnt snail-shell and rock salt mixed with honey;
one *niṣka* each of these quickly destroys even severe *grahaṇī* disease.

One should give to Dugdheṃduśāka a mixture of *kṛśānu*, the two types of *jājī*, honey, and the three pungents (*kaṭutraya*), combined with *cāṅgerikā*, the two types of *jīraka*, and coriander (*dhānya*), served lukewarm with curd.
Purging, abdominal pain, and frequent vomiting,
along with the contraction of the hands, feet, and other limbs, are the symptoms of all types of indigestion (ajīrṇa).
[The Ajīrṇakaṇṭaka-rasa]:
Take equal parts of purified mercury, poison, and sulfur, and grind them all together;
add black pepper in an amount equal to the total, and mix with the juice of the fruits of Kaṇṭakārī.
One should rub and saturate everything twenty-one times;
one should eat a pill the size of three *guñjā* seeds for the pacification of all indigestion.
This juice, known as *ajīrṇakaṇṭaka*, destroys cholera (*viṣūcikā*);
one should drink it after grinding the root of *tilaparṇī* with water.
Having ground [mercury] with sulphur and borax, and then treating it seven times with water from *jāti* fruits,
the perfected elixir named Vidhvaṃsana is a pacifier of cholera.

Nine *guñjā* seeds, combined with sugar, should be administered to him to destroy *viṣūcī*; for his food here, boiled rice with buttermilk is wholesome, and indeed, *vāstuka* greens are recommended as a vegetable.
[The Elixir for Conquering Cholera (Viṣūcīvijayarasa): Having ground equal parts of mercury, sulfur, and the ash of *ṭaṅka* (calamine), and having processed it seven times with nutmeg (*jātīphala*),
one who eats churned curd-rice and consumes nine *raktika*s of this mixture with sugar conquers cholera.
[The Elixir of the Fire-Boy]:
One pala each of mercury and sulfur, processed with the juices of *haṃsapādī*,
along with one kola of powdered poison, is cooked in a *vālukāyantra*.
One should mix half a pala of hemp with half a pala of black pepper;
this "Agnikumāra" is an appetite stimulant, especially effective for disorders of the digestive tract (grahaṇī).
It removes diseases born of wind and phlegm in an instant,
and it destroys fevers of the *sannipāta* type, dyspnea, consumption, and cough.
[The Mercury of the Mare’s Fire (Vaḍabāgniras):
There should be three *karṣas* each of *ṭaṅkaṇa*, black pepper, and *tuttha*;
twelve *niṣkas* of *sundara* mercury, and thirty *niṣkas* of iron dross.
Having mixed these powders together, one should place them in a clean vessel;
a man with a purified body should drink this after his meal.
First one should eat wholesome food, then only a small amount, and thereafter one may partake of betel;
thus the digestive fire of this man becomes equal to the submarine fire (vaḍavāgni). What more need be said here? For men, it is like a rejuvenative elixir (rasāyana).
Iron rust, rubbed with lotus juice, cooked in a sealed crucible (puṭapāka) in the juice of varā,
and then rubbed seven times in the fresh juice of mārkava, becomes beautiful.
For purification, one should take one *karṣa* of mercury and an equal amount of the dust of moving and non-moving [minerals], turn them into a collyrium, and grind them with cow’s milk for a day.

Having sealed this inside a crucible and placed it in a *kumbhapuṭa*, it becomes perfected; when cooled and ground by itself, it remains in a casket as the so-called *vaiśvānarapoṭalī*, which bestows the brilliance of a fierce fire.
This should be administered in doses of one *valla* each, using nineteen powders of black pepper mixed with clarified butter, while taking into account the strength of the patient's age.
For the sake of purifying the throat, one should consume excellent curd-rice in the measure of three mouthfuls, in order to pacify foul-smelling eructations.
Then at midday, one should eat food accompanied by ghee, curd, and side dishes; and at night, together with milk, or according to the requirements of the disease.
One should avoid split pulses that cause a burning sensation, those prepared with excessive salt or fried in oil,
as well as wood-apple (bilva), bitter gourd (kāravella), eggplant (vṛntāka), and sour gruel (kāñjika).
This indeed is called *poṭalī* by King Siṅghaṇa;
it destroys the entire multitude of diseases arising from weak digestion.
The procedures for the *poṭalī* preparations taught by Lokanātha have been specified here by the yogin Bhairavānanda for Siṃhaṇa.
These *poṭalīs* are illuminating and emollient; they are exceedingly beneficial for those with weak digestive fire. (VR 16.123)
Yellow in color, heavy and glossy, with a knot at the back and free from impurities—
that cowrie shell is indeed called *carācarā* by Nandin.
The best [image] measures one and a half niṣkas; the middling measures one niṣka;
and the lowest here, measuring three-quarters of a niṣka, is made of cowries.
Those that are inferior to them are fruitless, as are those that are coppery;
for having repeatedly bestowed their virtues, they indeed produce further disorders.

Having ground together mercury, iron ash, *vellahalinī*, the three pungents (*vyoṣa*), water, neem leaves, turmeric, and equal parts of salt, along with the juice of *bhṛṅga*, poison, *viṣatinduka*, and ginger, one should form pills the size of a *guñjā* seed. Once dried, this pill is known by the name *Vaḍavāmukhī*, prepared with silver (*tārā*). (VR 16.127)

Indeed, hunger is considered to be a prompter to wakefulness; it destroys all diseases, dispels disorders of phlegm, removes cough, heart disease, and asthma, alleviates colic, cures irregular appetite, pacifies abdominal tumors, uproots the pain of the roots [of the teeth], and removes swellings. What need is there for much talk?
It is the eradicator of every ailment.
[The Kravyādarasa]:
Having melted two palas of purified sulphur, one should add mercury measuring one pala, as well as dead copper and iron. VR 16.129.
Having reduced it by weight, one should place it upon a five-fingered leaf;
then, having carefully ground it, one should deposit it into an iron vessel.
Having carefully placed [the substance] in a crucible, one should ignite it with a gentle fire;
thus, one should properly dissolve the liquid of the citron to the measure of the vessel.
Having ground it with decoctions derived from the five pungent fruits (pañcakola) along with sour vetasa, one should indeed perform fifty saturations (bhāvanās). Thus, verse 16.132.
One should mix it with an equal amount of roasted *ṭaṅkaṇa* powder;
half of that [amount] is black salt (*kṛṣṇalavaṇa*), and long pepper (*marīcaka*) is equal to the total [of the other ingredients].
Thereafter, one should soak it seven times with water containing the alkaline ash of chickpea husks;
then, having dried it and ground it into a fine powder, one should place it inside a small jar.
Having eaten excessively large quantities of heavy meats and various heavy foods,
he consumed a broth measuring four *valla*s up to his throat.
One should drink it accompanied by pungent, sour, and buttermilk substances as a post-drink (anupāna);
thus, what has been eaten is quickly digested, and furthermore, it becomes an appetite stimulant (dīpana).
This essence was declared by Manthānabhairava to be the name of the flesh-eaters;
it was prescribed by the yogi Bhairavānanda upon reaching the village of King Siṅghaṇa, who was a great lover of meat.

This juice named Kravyāda stimulates digestion, promotes digestion, dries up malignant *āma*, destroys obesity of the abdomen, removes poison, and alleviates pain from the root [of the disease] and colic;

it destroys abdominal tumors (*gulma*) and splenic enlargement, annihilates malabsorption syndrome (*grahaṇī*), acts as a laxative, and removes wind-knots (*vātagranthi*) and enlargement of the belly. (VR 16.138)
One part of mercury, two parts of *vatsanābha* poison, an amount of *śivā* powder equal to the mercury, as well as sulfur and the three pungents (*tryūṣaṇa*). [Rājaśekharavaṭī] (VR 16.139)
Having ground it with great care, one should infuse it for seven days with the juice of betel leaves and the decoctions of *svarṇa* and *dhustūra*. Then,
having ground it into pills the size of chickpeas, one should dry them in the shade.

This medicinal pill, Rājaśekhara-vaṭī, combined with warm water, destroys weak digestion; it pacifies the afflictions of various types of great fevers, eradicates all root-causes [of disease], alleviates the pain of jaundice and abdominal enlargement, ends colic, promotes digestion, cures swelling, is expert at destroying the distress of wind (vāta), and annihilates diseases of phlegm (śleṣman).
[The Mercury-Boys Elixir: Pure mercury, poison, sulphur, the two alkalis, and the five salts—these ten ingredients in equal parts; and fresh *vijayā* (trumpetflower) roasted [with them]. 16.142.
An equal portion of the ten [ingredients] and half as much of *śigru* root—
all of this should be processed with the juices of *vijayā*, *śigru*, *citraka*, and *bhṛṅgarāja*.
One should grind it with fluxing agents for three days, seal it in a vessel,
and cook it gently over a lamp-like fire for one watch (yāma), until it is dry, then remove it.
The physician should saturate it seven times with the juice of fresh ginger and then powder it.
This is Dīpaka Agnikumāra; one niṣka of it should be licked with honey.
One karṣa of jaggery and dry ginger should be taken as an after-drink (anupāna) to stimulate digestion.
Amṛtavaṭī: Equal parts of kuṣṭha, gandhaka, viṣa, abhraka, triphalā, and pārada,
rubbed together with the urine of a deer, form the auspicious Amṛtavaṭī, to be taken in the measure of a green gram (mudga).
It destroys indigestion, phlegm, and wind; it stimulates the digestive fire and increases the appetite.
[The Mercury named Rākṣasa]:
Having thoroughly ground copper, mercury, sulphur, the three pungents (trikaṭu), sharp iron (tīkṣṇa), and black salt (sauvarcala) in a mortar, one should place it in a sand-pot for eight hours.

Once it has been steamed, one should mix in an equal amount of alkali derived from red śākinī plants; having processed the whole with the juice of citron (mātuluṅga), this is the mercury known by the name Rākṣasa.
In the past, Śaṅkara gave this [mantra] to his friend Cyavana, the sage whose digestive fire was sluggish, who had lost his vigor and whose sacrificial offerings were meager;

he, in turn, took it and offered it to Sūrya, the teacher of all the worlds—to that [Sūrya] be homage. Furthermore, at the time of giving this [mantra], one should avoid eight *guñjā* seeds even for mortals.
[The elixir named Jīvana]:

Take mercury, sulfur, rock salt, black salt, and borax; then, in successive order, add chebulic myrobalan, citrullus colocynthis, long pepper, and the fruit of *kataka*. These should be powdered and processed through repeated saturation with the juice of *bṛhatī*.
By means of successive saturation with the juices of ginger, asafoetida, punarnavā, pūtīka, and chinnarasa,
one should mix therein a twentieth part of the ingredient, according to the rules of measurement, in a quantity equal to that juice.
This mercury-elixir named Dīpanajīvana indeed destroys all indigestion, phlegm, wind, anemia, edema, halīmaka, jaundice, and colic; it stimulates the digestive fire and restores vitality.
[The Mercury of the Mare’s Fire]:
Take one part each of copper, orpiment, sulphur, sea-foam, *agnigarbha*, iron filings, the various salts, gold leaf, blue antimony, and *tutthaka*.

To these, twelve parts of mercury are added and slowly rubbed for a day with the juice of *vallī* and clarified butter. This perfected *vaḍavānala* (mare’s fire) cures all diseases when processed in a *gajapuṭa* (elephant-seal) furnace.
[The pill that generates fire:

Equal parts of long pepper, ginger, sulfur, mercury, poison, and black pepper, combined with the juice of *lakucha* and made into pills the size of a chickpea, quickly generate digestive fire. (VR 16.153)
[Sarvarogāntakā Vaṭī]:
Pure mercury, poison, sulphur, ajamoda, the three fruits (triphalā), sarjikṣāra, yavakṣāra, citraka, rock salt, and cumin. VR 16.154.
Equal parts of sauvarcala salt, viḍaṅga, sea salt, and the three pungents (tryūṣaṇa),
along with an amount of viṣamuṣṭi equal to the sum of all these, should be ground with the sour juice of jambīra fruit.
One should eat a pill with the luster of a mirage to pacify sluggish digestion;
thereafter, one should always consume half a pala each of harītakī, ginger, and jaggery.
This pill, renowned as the destroyer of all families of diseases, is celebrated for the treatment of impaired digestion (agnimāndya).
[The general method: One should daily consume half a *niṣka* of powdered dead copper mixed with honey and equal parts of *kaṇā*, in order to rekindle a diminished digestive fire.
One should drink one pala each of fresh ginger juice and honey;
by eating ghee and meat as desired, the digestive fire becomes powerful.
VRṢ, 17 [Now, the treatment for dysuria, urinary calculi, and so forth]:
Pain first arises in the waist and the region of the abdomen.
Subsequently, there is obstruction and burning urine; these are the symptoms of the disease of urinary calculi (aśmarī).
Having diligently ground the mercury with double its quantity of sulphur,
one should carefully take vasu, punarnavā, vāsā, and śvetā.
One should saturate this with those juices individually for three days each;
once cooked and dried inside a crucible, one should subject it to sudation using a water-press (*jalayantra*).
One should employ this plant named *pāṣāṇabhedin* along with its creeper; having ground it with the milk of *gopālakarkaṭī* and the root of *bhūmyāmalaka*,
one should administer it with water decocted with *kulattha*.
[The second *pāṣāṇabhedin* elixir: One should rub the juice of white *varṣābhū* with twice its amount of sulfur and cook it in a crucible; one should consume two *māṣa* grains of that.
One should drink the root of *pātālakarkaṭī* with water boiled from *kulattha* beans as an after-drink; at night, one should drink a decoction of the roots of *gokaṇṭaka* and *sadābhadra*.
This elixir, known by the name *pāṣāṇabhinnā*, is a stone-breaker (*pāṣāṇabhedaka*).
For one who drinks the powder produced from the seeds of *gokṣura*,
combined with sheep’s milk and mixed with the best of juices, the stone dissolves into powder and passes away.
[Trivikrama-rasa:
Equal amounts of copper and dead (calcined) goat’s milk should be cooked until the liquid has evaporated.
Then, that copper, pure mercury, and sulfur—each in equal parts—[should be combined].

Having ground that ball with the juices extracted from *nirguṇḍī* for one day, one should seal it and cook it for one watch (*yāma*) in a *vālukāyantra*; it should then be administered in a dose of two *guñjā*s.
One should administer the root of the *bījapūra* with water as an after-drink;
this juice, known by the name Trivikrama, destroys urinary calculi within one month.
One should burn in a closed crucible all these ingredients in equal proportions: *ānandabhairavīvaṭī*, sesame seeds, stalks of *apāmārga*, *kāravelī*, barley, and wood of *palāśa*.
One should administer a pill called Ānandabhairavī, made from one niṣka of that [mercury] with goat urine;
it destroys urinary calculi within seven days—of this there is no doubt.
[The general remedy: The root of *phalikā*, when ground with water, removes urinary calculi (*aśmarī*).
And barley-alkali, when licked with honey, should be a remover of urinary calculi.
Or one should drink one karṣa of turmeric and jaggery with fermented rice-water (cāraṇāla).
One who eats one karṣa of the root of vandhyākarkoṭakī combined with honey and sugar undoubtedly destroys urinary calculi; this has been declared by Śiva.
Emaciation, burning sensations, wasting of the limbs, excessive urination,
and a general malaise in all parts of the body are the symptoms of *mūtrameha*.
Taking the powder of *mārkaṇḍī* along with jaggery, one should consume it at night.
[Laghulokeśvararasa] Take one part of dead mercury (mṛtasūta) and four parts of purified sulfur; having ground them together with a cowrie shell, add one-quarter part of borax (ṭaṅkaṇa).
Having ground [the ingredients] with milk and sealed the mouth [of the crucible], one should fill the cowrie shells and roast them in a *puṭa* fire;
once cooled to the touch of the body, one should powder them—this is the *Laghulokeśvara* elixir.

This juice of four guñjās, nineteen black peppers, and one pala of jasmine root should be ground with goat’s milk; having drunk it subsequently, sweetened with sugar, it is the supreme remedy for dysuria.
There are eighteen types of barren women, proclaimed as being of nine kinds;
among them, the first type of barren woman is produced by sinful karma.
Through blood and through the individual humors, as well as all of them combined, it becomes fivefold;
and due to elemental spirits, deities, and malevolent spells, three types of barren women are proclaimed.
A man may also become sterile due to these defects of the semen.
The first is known as one who miscarries; the second is one whose children die;
the third is she who gives birth to daughters; and the "crow-barren" woman is she who bears only once.
Gold, silver, copper, and the essence of *tāpya* ore, as well as processed mercury—
each one in the measure of one *niṣka*— having been thoroughly purified and melted down.
This mercury, having been processed four times, should be mixed with twice its weight of sulfur and ground with the juices of *lakṣmaṇā* and the sap of *bandhujīva*.
Then, having placed it in a glass flask, one should set a copper vessel upon its mouth;
one should plaster the entire exterior of the flask with clay to a thickness of one finger-breadth.
Having dried it and placed the crucible back on the ground,
one should apply a *gajākhya* (elephant-named) *puṭa* using blue lotuses weighing one *śāṇa* or *karṣa*.

Once it has cooled to the temperature of one's own body, one should grind it into a powder and then saturate it seven times with the juice of *lakṣmaṇā*, drying it each time before placing it inside a casket.
This supreme elixir, combined with the powder of *aśvagandhā* and copper, mixed with cow’s milk and equal parts of *guñjā* and sugar, when consumed, is most excellent.
By employing this for three months, a barren woman becomes the mother of sons;
and for a woman who already has sons, she becomes purified by bathing [with the collyrium] from the eyes of Jaratkauśika.
Having prepared it with cow-ghee, one should indeed feed him at that time;
this should be given at every ritual occasion for as long as three months have passed.
This very king of mercury was described by the lords of yogis dwelling in the Campaka forest,
who were known by the name Pūrṇāmṛta, as Jayasundara.
When this elixir is consumed by women, the disease of childbirth shall not occur;
they shall give birth to sons who are long-lived, wise, and adorned with good fortune.
The diamond, emerald, ruby, blue flower-gem, beryl, then the go-meda, pearl, and likewise coral; these are the supreme essences of the precious portions.
All gems measuring five guñjās should be reduced to ashes with great effort, using the supreme method of successive division as prescribed in that tantra.
The ash derived from vaikrānta is eight times more potent than all others;
the ash produced from tāpya is equal to that, and the ash of vimala is likewise.
Having thoroughly ground together equal parts of mercury, sulfur, and collyrium— each three times the quantity of the others— one should mix them all with goat’s milk for two days.
Having carefully prepared a parpaṭī tablet and having ground it with great effort,
one should thoroughly rub it with a decoction of the leaves of *vandhyākarkoṭakī*.
One should seal it with twenty *kānanotpala* flowers sixteen times;
thus the mercury is perfected, known by the name Ratnabhāgottara.
It bestows progeny upon all women, including those who are barren or severely so;
it is prescribed in the Devīśāstra as the remedy for the disease of sterility in men.

This [preparation] is digestive, appetizing, and improves the sense of taste; it is aphrodisiac and destroys all diseases of pregnant women. It promotes sexual pleasure, cures the severe afflictions of anemia, and is auspicious. It bestows intelligence, produces sons, and grants good fortune to women. Being free from defects, it removes diseases of the reproductive organs and, through its application, alleviates every kind of suffering.
One *pala* of sulfur, and one *akṣa* each of realgar and orpiment, should be rubbed together for three days and then fashioned into an auspicious collyrium (*kajjalī*). (Cakribandharasa) 18.23.
Then, one should place the collyrium into a crucible shaped like a horn,
and subsequently, one should set a disc of two palas of copper upon its opening.
Having firmly compressed it with great effort until the joints are dried,
one should then properly effect the cooking by means of half a hollowed palm.
Having extracted it while naturally cold, one should grind it into a powder;
having strained it with a cloth, one should place it inside a small jar.
This *cakrikābandha* elixir, prepared with medicinal herbs that cure various diseases,
should be administered in cases of colic, abdominal tumors, and fistula-in-ano.
In cases of malabsorption syndrome, impaired digestion, abscesses, abdominal diseases, as well as elephantiasis, upward-moving wind, and intestinal obstruction, [this is indicated].
By means of his inexhaustible compassion, for the sake of protecting the three worlds...
